Further isolated evidence now retained in /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/plsneuro/output/brain-display/projection-17. Orthographic projection removes a large apparent bilateral scale imbalance (same original inflated geometry/value hashes: perspective widths 380/506 pixels, orthographic 536/532), but does not remove fine grain. Setting application map opacity to zero removes most remaining grain; use this to separate underlay geometry/lighting from varying overlay composition. A white/magenta coverage diagnostic shows broad missing regions, not the pervasive fine grain. Its run exits after writing the second image because white valid cortex violates the ordinary nonwhite-ink connected-component guard; do not call that diagnostic a full probe pass. Raising the independent analytical gray-ramp atlas width from 1024 to 4096 leaves no-mipmap RMSE unchanged (0.295954/0.369964/0.405660 at 8192/32768/131072 triangles). Large atlas width alone is not the remaining cause.

Consumer has now adopted only bounded native c14b36ac camera/depth/lifecycle and constant-color UV/update backports, exact candidate af5c235466be1f0dde445a73eba45ee76456f06e9733c45a49ef995c66c3ff7c on fd992a0c. Current consumer sources compile, display-state checks pass, and real beta/FIR each pass 12 hidden cases on ordinary JavaFX 24.0.1, preserving projected-value hashes and both camera modes. No OpenJFX override adopted. Root visual review still rejects default dark lighting and conspicuous grain; this native defect remains open. No native source edit or reservation taken in this record-only stint.
